alt: A belief held by faith or habit becomes a perspective once reasons and evidence are set out. A spectrum runs from universalism, where some values apply everywhere, to cultural relativism, where values are understood within each culture, with the 1993 Vienna Declaration holding both ideas in the middle. Definitions of value, secular and tolerance follow.
caption: Present universalism and relativism as perspectives with reasons, not as right and wrong.

after: ## Perspectives: why people hold different values
alt: Three groups on whether large shops should open on the day of rest: religious groups and some non-religious families favour closure; small shop owners prefer it; shop workers are divided; free-choice supporters and large retailers favour opening. The Sunday Trading Act 1994 lets large shops open for six hours, balancing values.
caption: Perspectives on one issue come from faith, family, money and freedom, not just religion.

alt: Six sources of a person’s values surround a central hub: upbringing and family, religion or belief, culture and history, economic position, personal experience and generation. Below, causes of value disagreements: different teachings, generational change, migration, economic change and media, and laws written when beliefs were more shared.
caption: Explain why someone holds a value before judging it.

alt: An arrow from survival priorities to self-expression shows Ronald Inglehart’s argument that, as societies become more economically secure, priorities shift towards personal freedom and tolerance, drawing on the World Values Survey first carried out in 1981. Strength: decades of repeated surveys. Limitations: links not cause, and critics say it treats one path as normal for all.
caption: A well-evidenced theory can still show correlation rather than cause.

alt: Eighty dots, 28 shaded, show that 28 of 80 members of a fictional Ardley youth club (35%) volunteered in the past year. Tested against the claim that young people don’t care about their community, the evidence fails: there is no comparison with older people, the sample is only club members, and informal help may be missed.
caption: Without a comparison group, one figure cannot support a generalisation.

alt: UDHR Articles 18 (freedom of religion) and 19 (freedom of expression) can pull against each other. A table evaluates the UDHR, the ICCPR and a June 2025 Pew report. Using Pew’s global estimate of about 24.2% religiously unaffiliated to argue one country’s rest-day law is outdated is reliable evidence used with weak reasoning.
caption: Check that a reliable figure actually connects to the conclusion drawn from it.

alt: Denmark passed a law in December 2023, by 94 votes to 77, protecting religious objects from public destruction with a fine or up to two years in prison; the government cited security and critics cited freedom of expression. Other actions: compromise laws, dialogue groups and flexible policies such as menu choices or festival time off.
caption: Contested actions should be presented with both sides’ reasons.
